stati.ente: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS)
stati.titolo: Florida Motor Vehicle Repair Act: Estimate & Invoice Checklist
stati.intro: In Florida the rules for repair shops are in the Florida Motor Vehicle Repair Act, part of chapter 559 of the Florida Statutes. A shop prepares a written estimate when the repair will cost the customer more than $150, gives an invoice when any repair is completed, and registers with the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services before doing business.

fatti.valore: Written estimate when the repair work will cost more than $150
fatti.breve: Written, for work over $150
fatti.nota: The estimate is a form with a list of required items, prepared before any diagnostic work or repair. The customer can decline it only by checking and signing the statement the statute prints in capital letters.

citazioni.testo: When any customer requests a motor vehicle repair shop to perform repair work on a motor vehicle, the cost of which repair work will exceed $150 to the customer, the shop shall prepare a written repair estimate, which is a form setting forth the estimated cost of repair work, including diagnostic work, before effecting any diagnostic work or repair.

Except as provided in subsection (5), a copy of the written repair estimate required by subsection (1) and the disclosure statement required by subsection (2) shall be given to the customer before repair work is begun.

fatti.valore: Customer approval before charging more than the estimate plus $10 or 10 percent, whichever is greater, up to $50
fatti.breve: To go past the estimate by more than $10 or 10 percent, whichever is greater (at most $50)
fatti.nota: The shop notifies the customer of the additional work and its estimated cost; the customer authorizes, modifies or cancels the order, orally or in writing.

citazioni.testo: It shall be unlawful for a motor vehicle repair shop to charge more than the written estimate plus $10 or 10 percent, whichever is greater, but not to exceed $50, unless the motor vehicle repair shop has obtained authorization to exceed the written estimate in accordance with subsection (1).

the customer shall be promptly notified by telephone, telegraph, mail, or other means of the additional repair work and estimated cost thereof. A customer so notified shall, orally or in writing, authorize, modify, or cancel the order for repair.

fatti.valore: A legible invoice when any repair is completed
fatti.breve: On completion of any repair
fatti.nota: The invoice can be on the same form as the written estimate. Its required contents are in the checklist below, including the shop registration number.

citazioni.testo: The motor vehicle repair shop shall provide each customer, upon completion of any repair, with a legible copy of an invoice for such repair. The invoice may be provided on the same form as the written repair estimate and shall include the following information:

fatti.valore: Inspection or return of removed parts, if the customer asks when the work is authorized
fatti.breve: On request made when the work is authorized
fatti.nota: The estimate form carries a statement that lets the customer say whether replaced parts are to be saved. Return does not apply where the shop has a warranty arrangement or an exchange parts program.

citazioni.testo: Upon request made at the time the repair work is authorized by the customer, the customer is entitled to inspect parts removed from her or his vehicle or, if the shop has no warranty arrangement or exchange parts program with a manufacturer, supplier, or distributor, have them returned to her or him.

fatti.valore: Registration with the department before doing business: $50, $150 or $300 a year for each location
fatti.breve: State registration, $50 to $300 a year per location
fatti.nota: The fee depends on how many employees perform repairs at the place of business (1 to 5, 6 to 10, 11 or more) and the registration is renewed biennially. The statute exempts an individual with no employees and no established place of business.

citazioni.testo: Each motor vehicle repair shop engaged or attempting to engage in the business of motor vehicle repair work must register with the department prior to doing business in this state.
If the place of business has 1 to 5 employees who perform repairs: $50.
If the place of business has 6 to 10 employees who perform repairs: $150.
If the place of business has 11 or more employees who perform repairs: $300.
Each registration must be renewed biennially on or before the expiration date of the current registration.
No registration application or fee is required for an individual with no employees and no established place of business.

fatti.valore: Estimates and invoices kept and open to the customer for at least 12 months
fatti.breve: At least 12 months
fatti.nota: The statute speaks of the customer’s right to inspect and copy the records; department staff can inspect them during business hours.

citazioni.testo: Each motor vehicle repair shop shall maintain repair records which shall include written repair estimates and repair invoices. A customer’s records shall be available to the customer for inspection and copying for a period of at least 12 months.

voci.testo: The name, address, and telephone number of the motor vehicle repair shop.
The name, address, and telephone number of the customer.
The date and time of the written repair estimate.
The year, make, model, odometer reading, and license tag number of the motor vehicle.
The proposed work completion date.
A general description of the customer’s problem or request for repair work or service relating to the motor vehicle.
A statement as to whether the customer is being charged according to a flat rate or an hourly rate, or both.

The estimated cost of repair which must include any charge for shop supplies or for hazardous or other waste removal and, if a charge is included, the estimate must include the following statement: “This charge represents costs and profits to the motor vehicle repair facility for miscellaneous shop supplies or waste disposal.”
If a charge is mandated by state or federal law, the estimate must contain a statement identifying the law and the specific amount charged under the law.
The charge for making a repair price estimate or, if the charge cannot be predetermined, the basis on which the charge will be calculated.
The customer’s intended method of payment.
The name and telephone number of another person who may authorize repair work, if the customer desires to designate such person.
A statement indicating what, if anything, is guaranteed in connection with the repair work and the time and mileage period for which the guarantee is effective.
A statement allowing the customer to indicate whether replaced parts should be saved for inspection or return.
A statement indicating the daily charge for storing the customer’s motor vehicle after the customer has been notified that the repair work has been completed.

If the cost of repair work will exceed $150, the shop must present to the customer a written notice conspicuously disclosing, in a separate, blocked section, only the following statement, in capital letters of at least 12-point type:
PLEASE READ CAREFULLY, CHECK ONE OF THE STATEMENTS BELOW, AND SIGN:
I UNDERSTAND THAT, UNDER STATE LAW, I AM ENTITLED TO A WRITTEN ESTIMATE IF MY FINAL BILL WILL EXCEED $150.
I REQUEST A WRITTEN ESTIMATE.
I DO NOT REQUEST A WRITTEN ESTIMATE AS LONG AS THE REPAIR COSTS DO NOT EXCEED $
THE SHOP MAY NOT EXCEED THIS AMOUNT WITHOUT MY WRITTEN OR ORAL APPROVAL.
I DO NOT REQUEST A WRITTEN ESTIMATE.

It shall be unlawful for a motor vehicle repair shop to charge more than the written estimate plus $10 or 10 percent, whichever is greater, but not to exceed $50, unless the motor vehicle repair shop has obtained authorization to exceed the written estimate in accordance with subsection (1).
the customer shall be promptly notified by telephone, telegraph, mail, or other means of the additional repair work and estimated cost thereof
A customer so notified shall, orally or in writing, authorize, modify, or cancel the order for repair.
Always give the customer a copy of any document requiring their signature.
The current date and odometer reading of the motor vehicle.
A statement indicating what was done to correct the problem or a description of the service provided.

An itemized description of all labor, parts, and merchandise supplied and the costs thereof, indicating what is supplied to the customer without cost or at a reduced cost because of a shop or manufacturer’s warranty.
A statement identifying any replacement part as being used, rebuilt, or reconditioned, as the case may be.
A statement indicating what, if anything, is guaranteed in connection with the repair work and the time and mileage period for which the guarantee is effective.
The registration number from the certificate issued by the department pursuant to this part.

Upon request made at the time the repair work is authorized by the customer, the customer is entitled to inspect parts removed from her or his vehicle or, if the shop has no warranty arrangement or exchange parts program with a manufacturer, supplier, or distributor, have them returned to her or him.
Each motor vehicle repair shop engaged or attempting to engage in the business of motor vehicle repair work must register with the department prior to doing business in this state.
Each initial application for registration must be accompanied by copies of the applicant’s estimate and invoice forms.

The sign shall contain the toll-free telephone number of the department for consumer information and assistance and shall inform customers that they may request, at the time the work order is taken, the return or inspection of all parts that have been replaced during the motor vehicle repair.
Each motor vehicle repair shop shall maintain repair records which shall include written repair estimates and repair invoices.

faq.q: What does the Florida Motor Vehicle Repair Act require from a repair shop?
faq.a: The sections read for this page require a shop to register with the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services before doing business, to prepare a written estimate when repair work will cost the customer more than $150, to get the customer’s authorization before charging more than the estimate plus $10 or 10 percent, whichever is greater, but not more than $50, and to give a legible invoice when any repair is completed.

faq.q: How much is the Florida motor vehicle repair shop registration?
faq.a: The statute sets the registration fee for each location on a per-year basis: $50 if the place of business has 1 to 5 employees who perform repairs, $150 with 6 to 10, and $300 with 11 or more. Each registration is renewed biennially. The statute calls it a registration, not a license.

faq.ricerca: can a mechanic charge more than the estimate
faq.q: Can a mechanic charge more than the estimate in Florida?
faq.a: The statute makes it unlawful for a motor vehicle repair shop to charge more than the written estimate plus $10 or 10 percent, whichever is greater, but not to exceed $50, unless the shop has obtained authorization to exceed the written estimate. The customer is notified of the additional repair work and its estimated cost and authorizes, modifies or cancels the order.

stati.legge: Automotive Repair Act (as explained in BAR’s Write It Right guide)
stati.titolo: California Auto Repair Laws: BAR Estimate & Invoice Rules
stati.intro: In California repair shops are automotive repair dealers registered with the Bureau of Automotive Repair (BAR). This page quotes BAR’s own guide for dealers, Write It Right, which summarizes the Automotive Repair Act and its regulations and gives the legal reference after each rule: an estimate before any repair, the customer’s authorization recorded on it, and an invoice when the job is completed.

fatti.valore: An estimate before an automotive repair dealer performs any repair
fatti.breve: Required before any repair
fatti.nota: The guide lists no dollar threshold. Certain preventative maintenance services are the exception it describes, when the service is free or its total price is displayed or acknowledged by the customer.

citazioni.testo: An estimate is required for an automotive repair dealer to perform repairs to a motor vehicle. (BPC § 9884.9)

An estimate must contain a description of the specific job and the estimated price for all parts and labor. Each part listed in the estimate shall be new unless specifically identified as a used, rebuilt, or reconditioned part. (BPC § 9884.9, CCR § 3353(a))

fatti.valore: Customer authorization, written, oral or electronic, recorded on the estimate before any repair and again before any additional repair
fatti.breve: Before any repair and before any additional repair
fatti.nota: A note left with a vehicle dropped off after hours is not an authorization, the guide says. For additional work the dealer prepares a revised work order and documents the new authorization on the work order and the invoice.

citazioni.testo: All repairs must be authorized by the customer in written, oral, or electronic form. The authorization must be obtained and recorded on the estimate before beginning any repairs.

Authorization is required before beginning any repairs, even when a vehicle is dropped off before or after normal business hours along with a note requesting repairs to be performed. The note does not constitute authorization.
Before beginning any additional repairs beyond the original estimate, or having any additional charges accrue, complete the following steps:

fatti.valore: An invoice when all repairs for the job are completed
fatti.breve: On completion of all repairs
fatti.nota: Warranty repairs, repairs at no charge and preventative maintenance services are recorded on the invoice too.

citazioni.testo: The invoice is provided to the customer upon completion of all repairs for a specific job, including any preventative maintenance services defined in BPC § 9880.1(j). (BPC § 9884.8, CCR § 3356)

fatti.valore: Replaced parts returned if the customer asks when the estimate is authorized
fatti.breve: On request made when the estimate is authorized
fatti.nota: Core parts sold on an exchange basis and warranty parts are the exceptions; the customer is offered the chance to inspect them and the invoice records what could not be returned.

citazioni.testo: Yes, if requested by the customer at the time the estimate is authorized. However, core parts (such as a battery) that are sold on an exchange basis or parts that must be returned to the supplier under warranty are not required to be returned to the customer. In these circumstances, the customer must be offered the opportunity to inspect the replaced parts. Any replaced parts that cannot be returned to the customer must be recorded on the invoice. (BPC § 9884.10, CCR §§ 3355, 3356(i))

fatti.valore: Automotive repair dealer registration with BAR: application fee $200, annual renewal fee $200
fatti.breve: BAR registration, $200 and $200 a year to renew
fatti.nota: BAR calls it a license on its pages and lists its type as a registration. It is for the business: BAR writes that a license is not required to work as a general automotive repair mechanic.

citazioni.testo: Required to diagnose, service, or repair vehicles for compensation. This includes mobile, referral, or sublet repair services.
Application fee: $200
Annual renewal fee: $200
A BAR license is not required to work as a general automotive repair mechanic.

fatti.valore: Invoices, estimates and work orders kept for at least three years
fatti.breve: At least three years
fatti.nota: Paper or electronic form; each record carries an identifier that links it to its transaction.

citazioni.testo: Records must be maintained for at least three years and shall be open for reasonable inspection and/or reproduction by BAR during normal business hours. (BPC § 9884.11, CCR §§ 3340.15(e), 3358(d))

checklist.titolo: On the estimate and the work order

voci.testo: An estimate must contain a description of the specific job and the estimated price for all parts and labor.
Each part listed in the estimate shall be new unless specifically identified as a used, rebuilt, or reconditioned part.

any charges associated with the handling, management, and disposal costs of toxic wastes or hazardous substances directly related to the specific job must be itemized separately in both the estimate and the invoice
The automotive repair dealer must include with the estimate a statement of any sublet repair to be performed on the vehicle.
Charging for items generally noted as shop supplies or miscellaneous parts is prohibited.
sales tax is only included in the invoice
A work order must contain the authorized estimate for a specific job, the repairs requested and authorized by the customer, and the vehicle’s odometer reading.
Written authorization consists of the customer’s signature and the date the customer authorized the repairs.
Oral authorization consists of the date, time, name of the person authorizing the repairs, and telephone number called, if any.
Electronic authorization consists of the date, time, name of the person authorizing the repairs, and email address or phone number (text messaging) contacted, if any.
The customer must be provided a copy of any document requiring their signature at the time of signing.
Prepare a revised work order that describes all additional parts and labor, provides the cost of all additional parts and labor, and includes the total revised cost.
Contact the customer by phone, email, text, or other electronic means to provide all the information listed in the revised work order and obtain the customer's authorization.
Properly document the customer’s authorization on both the work order and invoice.
The automotive repair dealer registration number and the corresponding business name and address as shown in BAR’s records.
An itemized list of all services and repairs performed and the prices for each. Include any diagnosis, warranty repairs, or repairs performed at no charge.
An itemized list of each part supplied. List each part in common terms so that the customer can understand what they purchased and the price of the part.
State if each part is new, used, reconditioned, rebuilt, and whether any crash parts are OEM or non-OEM aftermarket.
Replaced parts that cannot be returned to the customer, if applicable.
The subtotal price for all service and repair work performed.
The subtotal price for all parts supplied, not including sales tax.
The sales tax, if applicable.
The toxic waste fee charged, if any, as stated on the original estimate and the automotive repair dealer’s Environmental Protection Agency number.
The total cost for all service and repair work, parts supplied, and applicable sales tax.

However, core parts (such as a battery) that are sold on an exchange basis or parts that must be returned to the supplier under warranty are not required to be returned to the customer. In these circumstances, the customer must be offered the opportunity to inspect the replaced parts.
Any replaced parts that cannot be returned to the customer must be recorded on the invoice.
BAR licenses California's auto repair businesses.
Automotive repair dealers must post required signs for each license they hold.
Records must be maintained for at least three years and shall be open for reasonable inspection and/or reproduction by BAR during normal business hours.
all records associated with a specific transaction must have a unique identifier linking the records to that specific transaction

faq.q: What is BAR’s Write It Right?
faq.a: Write It Right is the Bureau of Automotive Repair’s guide to the documentation and authorization requirements for automotive repair dealers: estimates, authorizations, invoices and records. BAR describes it as a quick reference that is not all-inclusive, with the statutory and regulatory references after each rule. This page quotes it and links to it.

faq.q: Does an auto repair shop need a Bureau of Automotive Repair license in California?
faq.a: BAR writes that the automotive repair dealer license is required to diagnose, service, or repair vehicles for compensation, including mobile, referral, or sublet repair services. Its type is a registration, with an application fee of $200 and an annual renewal fee of $200. BAR also writes that a BAR license is not required to work as a general automotive repair mechanic.

faq.q: What do California auto repair laws require on an estimate?
faq.a: According to BAR’s guide, an estimate is required for an automotive repair dealer to perform repairs to a motor vehicle, and it must contain a description of the specific job and the estimated price for all parts and labor. Each part listed is new unless specifically identified as used, rebuilt, or reconditioned. The customer’s authorization is recorded on the estimate before any repair begins.

stati.legge: Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Act
stati.titolo: Michigan Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Act: Shop Checklist
frasi: michigan motor vehicle service and repair act
stati.intro: Michigan’s rules are in the Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Act. A repair facility registers with the state, gives the customer a written, itemized estimate before beginning repair work, returns replaced parts, and hands over a written statement when the repaired vehicle goes back to the customer.

fatti.valore: Written, itemized estimate before beginning repair work, unless the customer signs the waiver printed in the act
fatti.breve: Written and itemized, before the work
fatti.nota: The waiver is a fixed text in 14 point or larger bold capital type, with the amount the customer agrees to pay without an estimate. The cost of a diagnosis goes in the written estimate before the diagnosis is made.

citazioni.testo: Before beginning repair work, a motor vehicle repair facility shall give to the customer a written estimate that itemizes as closely as possible the price for labor and parts necessary for the work.
The waiver must be in 14 point or larger bold capital type face and executed with 1 copy to the customer who is requesting the repairs.

fatti.valore: Written or oral consent before charging above the estimate; none needed for an excess of not more than 10% or $50.00, whichever is lesser
fatti.breve: To exceed the estimate by more than 10% or $50.00, whichever is lesser
fatti.nota: The small-excess rule applies when no waiver was signed and unless the customer specifically asked to be consulted. With a waiver, the limit is the amount the customer stated.

citazioni.testo: A facility shall not charge for work done or parts supplied in excess of the estimated price, or in excess of the limit stated by the customer in the waiver described in subsection (3), without the knowing written or oral consent of the customer

If a waiver is not signed under subsection (3) and the estimated price is exceeded by not more than 10% or $50.00, whichever is lesser, the facility is not required to obtain the written or oral consent of the customer for the excess charge unless specifically requested by the customer.

fatti.valore: A written statement to each customer when the repaired vehicle is returned
fatti.breve: Written statement on return of the vehicle
fatti.nota: The act does not call it an invoice. It is signed for the facility and names the mechanic or mechanics who did the diagnosis and the repair.

citazioni.testo: shall give to each customer a written statement upon return of the repaired vehicle to the customer

The statement shall be signed by the owner of the facility or by a person designated by the owner to represent the facility. The name of the mechanic or mechanics who performed the diagnosis and the repair shall also appear on the statement.

fatti.valore: Replaced parts returned to the customer when the repair work is completed, with a printed notice of that right
fatti.breve: Returned at completion; notice required
fatti.nota: The exceptions are parts exempted for size or weight, warranty or exchange parts, and containers that held flammable fuels. The notice goes on the work order or on a sign with lettering not less than 1 inch high.

citazioni.testo: A motor vehicle repair facility shall return replaced parts to the customer at the time the repair work is completed.

A facility that displays the notice described in subsection (2) on a clearly legible sign with lettering not less than 1 inch high, conspicuously displayed in the part of the facility where customers routinely contract for repairs, is not required to provide the notice to a customer in the form of a document described in subsection (2).

fatti.valore: Registration of the facility with the state administrator; registration number on every document used with the public
fatti.breve: State registration, number on every document
fatti.nota: In the act the administrator is the secretary of state. The certificate of registration is displayed where customers can see it. Fees are not in the sections we read.

citazioni.testo: Unless the act or practice is otherwise exempt by this act, a person shall not engage in the business or activity of a motor vehicle repair facility unless the person registers the facility with the administrator pursuant to this act.
"Administrator" means the secretary of state or any individual designated by the secretary of state to act on behalf of the secretary of state.

A motor vehicle repair facility shall include the facility's registration number, as assigned by the administrator, on each copy of any instrument, form, contract, or other document used by the applicant in dealing with the public in the repair of motor vehicles

voci.testo: a written estimate that itemizes as closely as possible the price for labor and parts necessary for the work

The cost of a diagnosis made by the facility, whether or not the customer authorizes the facility to perform those repairs, must be included in the written estimate before the diagnosis is undertaken.

A motor vehicle repair facility shall include the facility's registration number, as assigned by the administrator, on each copy of any instrument, form, contract, or other document used by the applicant in dealing with the public in the repair of motor vehicles

checklist.titolo: If the customer waives the estimate

voci.testo: The waiver must be in 14 point or larger bold capital type face and executed with 1 copy to the customer who is requesting the repairs.
voluntarily authorize
to provide services or parts in the repair of the below described motor vehicle without receiving an estimate of repair costs. By signing this form, I understand that I will give up my right to:
1. Receive a written estimate of the cost for repairs;
2. Approve in advance any repairs or costs with a total cost under $
3. Refuse to pay for repairs with a total cost less than the amount stated above.
The facility may exceed the amount stated above only after I give my written or oral approval.

checklist.titolo: On the written statement given with the repaired vehicle

voci.testo: Repairs needed, as determined by the facility.
Repairs requested by the customer.
Repairs authorized by the customer.
The facility's estimate of repair costs.
The actual cost of repairs.
The repairs or services performed, including a detailed identification of all parts that were replaced and a specification as to which are new, used, rebuilt, or reconditioned.
A certification that the repairs were completed properly or a detailed explanation of an inability to complete repairs properly.
The statement shall be signed by the owner of the facility or by a person designated by the owner to represent the facility.
The name of the mechanic or mechanics who performed the diagnosis and the repair shall also appear on the statement.
A motor vehicle repair facility shall return replaced parts to the customer at the time the repair work is completed.

If a facility is obligated to return a replaced part to the manufacturer or a distributor under a warranty agreement, or, subject to subsection (4), under an exchange agreement, the facility is not required to return that part to the customer. However, the facility or mechanic shall offer the customer an opportunity to inspect the replaced part.

If a facility charges a fee to a customer in connection with the return of replaced parts, the facility shall disclose that fee to the customer in writing before the customer engages the facility to replace the part.

the facility shall keep the parts for not less than 2 business days after the customer takes possession of the repaired vehicle, unless the customer has specifically authorized immediate disposition of the parts

A customer must be informed of the customer's right to receive or inspect replaced parts as provided in this section before the customer executes any document or engages the facility or mechanic for the work.

YOU ARE ENTITLED BY LAW TO THE RETURN OF ALL PARTS REPLACED, EXCEPT THOSE WHICH ARE TOO HEAVY OR LARGE, AND THOSE REQUIRED TO BE SENT BACK TO THE MANUFACTURER OR DISTRIBUTOR BECAUSE OF WARRANTY WORK OR AN EXCHANGE AGREEMENT. YOU ARE ENTITLED TO INSPECT THE PARTS WHICH CANNOT BE RETURNED TO YOU.

A facility that displays the notice described in subsection (2) on a clearly legible sign with lettering not less than 1 inch high, conspicuously displayed in the part of the facility where customers routinely contract for repairs, is not required to provide the notice to a customer in the form of a document described in subsection (2).

Unless the act or practice is otherwise exempt by this act, a person shall not engage in the business or activity of a motor vehicle repair facility unless the person registers the facility with the administrator pursuant to this act.

Except for a motor vehicle repair facility that is an auxiliary facility, a motor vehicle repair facility shall at all times display, in a place and manner conspicuous to the facility's customers, a current and valid certificate of repair facility registration issued by the administrator.

The motor vehicle repair facility shall display a clearly legible sign in a conspicuous place at the entrance to the facility that indicates that customers may make inquiries concerning repair service or complaints to the administrator and states the address and telephone number of the department.

faq.ricerca: michigan motor vehicle service and repair act
faq.q: What does the Michigan Motor Vehicle Service and Repair Act require from a repair facility?
faq.a: In the sections read for this page, the act requires a facility to be registered, to give a written, itemized estimate before beginning repair work, to obtain the customer’s written or oral consent before charging more than the estimate (with a small-excess rule of not more than 10% or $50.00, whichever is lesser), to return replaced parts, and to give a written statement of the repairs when the vehicle is returned.

faq.q: Does a repair shop in Michigan need a repair facility license?
faq.a: The act speaks of registration: a person shall not engage in the business or activity of a motor vehicle repair facility unless the person registers the facility with the administrator, unless the act exempts the activity. The facility displays its certificate of registration and puts its registration number on every document used with the public. The fee is not in the sections we read.

faq.ricerca: can a mechanic charge more than the estimate
faq.q: Can a mechanic charge more than the estimate in Michigan?
faq.a: Not without the knowing written or oral consent of the customer, obtained after the facility finds the estimate insufficient and before the extra work is done. The act allows one case without consent: when no waiver was signed and the estimated price is exceeded by not more than 10% or $50.00, whichever is lesser, unless the customer specifically asked to be consulted.

stati.legge: Motor Vehicle Repair Shop Regulations (Part 82, published by DMV as CR-82)

stati.ente: Washington State Legislature (Revised Code of Washington)
stati.titolo: Washington State Auto Repair Laws: Estimate & Invoice Rules
stati.intro: Washington’s rules for repair shops are in chapter 46.71 of the Revised Code of Washington. Before providing parts or labor a repair facility gives a written price estimate or offers the customer the three alternatives the statute prints; parts and labor are recorded on an invoice whether or not an estimate was required.

fatti.valore: Written price estimate before providing parts or labor, or the customer’s signed choice among the three printed alternatives
fatti.breve: Written estimate or the customer’s signed choice
fatti.nota: Estimates above one hundred dollars are in writing and carry the listed information. No written estimate is required when the vehicle arrives without face-to-face contact, but the facility still needs the customer’s authorization first.

citazioni.testo: a repair facility prior to providing parts or labor shall provide the customer or the customer's designee with a written price estimate of the total cost of the repair, including parts and labor
all estimates that exceed one hundred dollars shall be in writing and include the following information

A written estimate shall not be required when the customer's motor vehicle or component has been brought to an automotive repair facility's regular place of business without face-to-face contact between the customer and the repair facility.

fatti.valore: Oral or written authorization before charging more than one hundred ten percent of the written estimate
fatti.breve: To go more than ten percent over the written estimate
fatti.nota: The limit is counted before retail sales tax. An oral authorization is noted on the estimate with the details listed in the checklist.

citazioni.testo: The repair facility may not charge the customer more than one hundred ten percent, exclusive of retail sales tax, of the total shown on the written price estimate. Neither of these limitations apply if, before providing additional parts or labor the repair facility obtains either the oral or written authorization of the customer, or the customer's designee, to exceed the written price estimate.

fatti.valore: An invoice for all parts and labor, given to the customer when the repairs are completed
fatti.breve: Always, on completion of the repairs
fatti.nota: The invoice repeats the information required on the estimate and adds the items in the checklist. Parts and labor need not be priced separately for an advertised special, a written repair menu item or a routine service package.

citazioni.testo: Whether or not a written estimate is required, parts and labor provided by an automotive repair facility shall be clearly and accurately recorded in writing on an invoice
A copy of the invoice shall be provided to the customer upon completion of the repairs.

fatti.valore: Replaced parts returned when the work is completed, if the customer asked when authorizing the repair
fatti.breve: On request made when the repair is authorized
fatti.nota: Parts under warranty or parts that go back to a distributor, remanufacturer or rebuilder are not returned; the facility offers to show them.

citazioni.testo: Except for parts covered by a manufacturer's or other warranty or parts that must be returned to a distributor, remanufacturer, or rebuilder, the repair facility shall return replaced parts to the customer at the time the work is completed if the customer requested the parts at the time of authorization of the repair.

fatti.valore: No registration specific to repair shops in chapter 46.71; the chapter refers to the Department of Revenue registration certificate
fatti.breve: None specific to repair shops in the chapter read
fatti.nota: The chapter does not set up a license or registration of its own for repair facilities. It mentions the registration certificate that the Department of Revenue issues to businesses, with a notice of these rules. Other state or local licenses are outside the pages we read.

citazioni.testo: When the department of revenue issues a registration certificate under RCW 82.32.030 to an automotive repair facility, it must give written notice to the person of the requirements of this chapter in a manner prescribed by the director of revenue, including by electronic means.

fatti.valore: Copies of written estimates and invoices kept for at least one year after the repairs
fatti.breve: At least one year
fatti.nota: Electronic records are allowed if the facility can print them on request.

citazioni.testo: Every automotive repair facility shall retain and make available for inspection, upon request by the customer or the customer's authorized representative, true copies of the written price estimates and invoices required under this chapter for at least one year after the date on which the repairs were performed.

Every automotive repair facility shall retain and make available for inspection, upon request by the customer or the customer's authorized representative, true copies of the written price estimates and invoices required under this chapter for at least one year after the date on which the repairs were performed.
The repair facility shall make available, upon request, a copy of any express warranty provided by the repair facility to the customer that covers repairs performed on the vehicle.

faq.q: What do Washington State auto repair laws require from a repair shop?
faq.a: Chapter 46.71 RCW requires a repair facility, before providing parts or labor, to give the customer a written price estimate or to offer the three alternatives printed in the statute; to obtain authorization before charging more than one hundred ten percent of the written estimate; to record parts and labor on an invoice; to return replaced parts if the customer asked for them when authorizing the repair; to post the customer rights sign; and to keep estimates and invoices for at least one year.

stati.ente: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
stati.titolo: Minnesota Auto Repair Laws: Written Estimate & Invoice Rules
stati.intro: Minnesota’s repair rules are in sections 325F.56 to 325F.66 of the Minnesota Statutes. They cover repairs of motor vehicles, appliances and dwelling places used primarily for personal, family or household purposes. A shop gives a written estimate when the customer asks for one, cannot charge more than 110 percent of it without a new authorization, and gives a dated invoice when the repairs are completed.

fatti.valore: Written estimate when the customer asks for one, before repairs start
fatti.breve: Written, on the customer’s request
fatti.nota: In these sections “repairs” means work for a total price of more than $100. The contents of the written estimate are in the definition quoted in the checklist. Telling the customer the contents aloud before starting, and handing over the writing at the end, also satisfies the requirement.

citazioni.testo: Upon the request of a customer for a written estimate and prior to the commencement of repairs, a shop shall provide the customer with a written estimate.

"Repairs" means work performed for a total price of more than $100, including the price of parts and materials, to restore a malfunctioning, defective, or worn motor vehicle, appliance, or dwelling place used primarily for personal, family, or household purposes and not primarily for business or agricultural purposes.

The requirement of a written estimate in sections 325F.56 to 325F.66 is fulfilled if a shop orally communicates the contents of a required writing to the customer prior to commencing repairs and provides the writing to the customer upon completion of the repairs.

fatti.valore: No charge for unauthorized repairs; a revised written estimate and a new authorization to go above 110 percent of the estimate
fatti.breve: To charge more than 110 percent of the estimate

the shop may charge more than 110 percent of the estimate for the repairs if the shop immediately provides the customer a revised written estimate pursuant to this section and receives authorization to continue with the repairs

fatti.valore: A dated invoice when the repairs are completed, for repair work of more than $50 and for any warranty, service contract or insurance work
fatti.breve: On completion, for repairs over $50
fatti.nota: If the customer collects the vehicle without face to face contact, the shop mails the invoice within two business days. A written estimate can serve as the invoice if the required information is written on its face.

citazioni.testo: Upon completion of repairs, a shop shall provide the customer with a copy of a dated invoice for the repairs performed.
any repair work performed for a total value of more than $50, including the price of parts and materials
A written estimate may be used as an invoice if the required invoice information is written on the face of the estimate.

fatti.valore: Replaced parts returned if the customer asks before repairs are commenced
fatti.breve: On request made before repairs start
fatti.nota: Warranty and exchange parts are not returned, but the customer can examine them for five business days after the repairs.

citazioni.testo: If a customer makes a request before repairs are commenced, the shop shall return replaced parts to the customer, except parts which the shop is required to return to the manufacturer, distributor, or other person under a warranty or exchange arrangement, is required to retain pursuant to law, or is necessary for pending litigation. The customer shall be given an opportunity to examine warranty or exchange parts for a period of five business days after completion of repairs.

fatti.breve: At least one year
fatti.nota: The customer can get a copy by paying reasonable reproduction costs.

faq.q: What do Minnesota auto repair laws require from a repair shop?
faq.a: Sections 325F.56 to 325F.66 require a shop to give a written estimate when the customer asks for one before repairs start, not to charge for unauthorized repairs, not to charge more than 110 percent of a written estimate without a revised estimate and a new authorization, to give a dated invoice on completion, to return replaced parts on a request made before the repairs, to keep records for at least one year and to display the sign quoted in the checklist.

faq.q: Can a mechanic charge more than the estimate in Minnesota?
faq.a: If the shop gave a written estimate, the statute says it shall not charge more than 110 percent of the total price stated in the estimate. It can charge more only if, after starting, it finds that additional work is necessary, did not unreasonably fail to disclose that possible need when it made the estimate, immediately gives the customer a revised written estimate and receives authorization to continue. The sign the statute requires adds that an oral estimate is not subject to these limits.

faq.a: No single template fits every state, because each state lists different items: the checklists on the state pages show the items word for word, with the section they come from, and can be printed and compared with the form a shop already uses. A form is not checked or approved by this site.

faq.q: What has to be on an auto repair estimate?
faq.a: Each state has its own list. In the states covered here the lists share a core: who the shop and the customer are, the vehicle, the problem or the work requested, and the price of parts and labor. Some states add statements that must be printed word for word. The state checklists give every item with its section.
